newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bubble fully inflated for Belgian bonds - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bubble fully inflated for Belgian bonds - dealers.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures were firmer, riding on the coattails of strength in the German market, but dealers said the demand, which was mainly professionally driven, would peter out.
By mid-morning prices were off their highs with dealers saying the market was running out of reasons to buy and some mild profit-taking was seen. Overall, volumes remained low.

Players were eyeing U.S. factory gate data due at the end of the week for new direction with forecasts centring on another batch of benign figures. Before that, there could be a brief upset from German unemployment figures.
Most players expected the data to show that unemployment stayed high, although some said talk of a fall in joblessness rather than a rise was behind this morning's profit-taking.

Front-month OLO futures were up 0.17 at 121.98 at 0925 GMT, off a high of 122.03, with 122.00 seen as an initial resistance level, 122.50 the next level and the historical high of 123.83 set in February as the third.

The benchmark 10-year OLO yielded 5.64 percent, down from 5.67 percent late on Friday. "We are seeing the bottom of the trading range...from here portfolios start selling, to take profits, to reduce their exposure," a trader said.
Dealers said they did not see much chance of the benchmark yield breaking below the historical low of 5.50 percent set on February 14 any time soon.

They said the longer end was better bid than 10-year OLOs. By comparison, the price of 10-year OLOs gained 11 basis points on Monday morning, but 15-year OLOs added 24 basis points and the 20-year paper rose by 30 basis points as players refocused on longer bonds amid continued signs of low, steady inflation.
